sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match, one word or complete the table).

questions.q: State True or False: (a) The RBI creates credit. (b) The RBI's headquarters is in Bengaluru.
questions.answer:
(a) False — commercial banks create credit.
(b) False — it is in Mumbai.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) A bank accepts ______ from the public. (b) A bank gives ______ to the public.
Give one word: (a) The claim to receive payment. (b) The fraction of deposits a bank must keep as cash.
Fill in the blanks: (a) The initial new deposit in a bank is the ______ deposit. (b) Deposits created by the bank's loans are ______ deposits.
Match: (a) SBI — ? (b) IFCI — ? [development bank / commercial bank]
Complete: A bank receives a deposit of ₹200 and lends ₹180. (a) Primary deposit = ? (b) Total deposit after the loan = ?

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: How does a bank create credit?
questions.answer: A bank keeps a fraction of each deposit as cash (CRR) and lends the rest. Each loan creates a new (secondary) deposit, which is again partly lent. Total credit = initial deposit × 1/CRR, e.g. ₹100 × 5 = ₹500 at a CRR of 20%.

questions.q: What is the meaning of banking?
questions.answer: Banking means accepting deposits of money from the public for lending or investment. The deposits are repayable on demand or otherwise and can be withdrawn by cheque, draft or order.

questions.q: Distinguish between a bank and banking.
questions.answer:
A bank is an institution that accepts deposits and gives loans.
Banking is the activity a bank carries on: accepting deposits for lending or investment, repayable on demand and withdrawable by cheque.

or.q: How does a bank keep valuables in safe custody?
or.answer: A bank provides locker facilities in which customers keep jewellery, property documents and other valuables safely, for a rent.

questions.q: What credit do development banks provide?
questions.answer: Development banks give long-term credit to private companies and public sector units to set up industries and build infrastructure, e.g. IDBI, IFCI and State Finance Corporations.

or.q: Distinguish between a lender and a borrower.
or.answer: The lender gives money as a loan and has the right to claim it back with interest, e.g. a bank. The borrower takes the loan now and promises to repay it later with interest.

questions.q: How many types of banks are there in India? Name them.
questions.answer: Four: (1) the Reserve Bank of India, the central bank; (2) commercial banks; (3) cooperative banks; (4) development banks.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: An urban unemployed person wants a loan to start a small business. Which bank should they approach and why?
questions.answer:
They should approach an urban cooperative bank (or a commercial bank).
Urban cooperative banks give credit for self-employment activities, small-scale industry and personal finance at reasonable terms.
Commercial banks also give loans to start businesses to people able to repay in future.

questions.q: Explain the working of commercial banks in India.
questions.answer:
Commercial banks accept deposits from the public and give loans to individuals and businesses.
They create credit through their lending and earn profit by charging interest and fees for drafts and money transfers.
They are in the public sector (SBI, PNB, Bank of Baroda) or the private sector (ICICI, HDFC, Yes Bank).

questions.q: Distinguish between a commercial bank and a cooperative bank.
questions.answer:
Commercial bank: a company in the public or private sector that aims at profit and serves the general public — SBI, HDFC.
Cooperative bank: run by a cooperative society under state laws for the mutual benefit of members. It gives credit in rural areas (farming, cattle, fishery) and urban areas (self-employment, small industry, consumer durables).

questions.q: What are development banks? Give examples.
questions.answer:
Development banks give long-term credit to private companies and public sector units to set up industries and create infrastructure, which economic development needs.
Examples: Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI), Industrial Finance Corporation of India (IFCI) and State Finance Corporations.

questions.q: Describe the steps in opening a savings account in a bank.
questions.answer:
(1) Visit the bank and ask for an account-opening form.
(2) Fill in the form with name, address and nominee details and attach photographs and proof of identity and address (KYC).
(3) Deposit the minimum initial amount.
(4) The bank opens the account, gives an account number and issues a passbook and cheque book for deposits and withdrawals.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: How does a bank create credit? Explain with a numerical example.
questions.answer:
A bank keeps a fraction of deposits as cash (CRR) and lends the rest; each loan becomes a new deposit.
Example with CRR 20%:
Round 1: A deposits ₹100; the bank keeps ₹20 and lends ₹80.
Round 2: ₹80 is deposited; the bank keeps ₹16 and lends ₹64.
Round 3: ₹64 is deposited; the bank keeps ₹12.80 and lends ₹51.20 … and so on.
Total credit = 100 × 1/20% = ₹500, made up of ₹100 cash reserve and ₹400 loans.
The primary deposit is ₹100; the secondary deposits total ₹400. A lower CRR creates more credit (10% gives ₹1,000).

questions.q: Explain the primary functions of a bank.
questions.answer:
(1) Accepting deposits: the bank opens an account with an account number, adds deposits and deducts withdrawals, pays interest on some deposits, and issues cheque books for withdrawals and payments.
(2) Giving loans: it lends to people who can repay in future — for TVs, refrigerators, cars and houses, or to start a business — and charges interest.
It also keeps valuables such as jewellery and documents safe in lockers.

questions.q: Write short notes on (a) the Reserve Bank of India and (b) cooperative banks.
questions.answer:
(a) RBI: the central bank and head of the banking system, with its headquarters in Mumbai. All banks follow its rules. It issues currency notes (except one-rupee notes and coins, which the Ministry of Finance issues) and acts as banker to the central and state governments.
(b) Cooperative banks: run by cooperative societies under state laws. Rural ones lend for farming, cattle and fishery; urban ones lend for self-employment, small industry, durable goods and personal finance. Examples are state cooperative banks, PACS, urban cooperative banks and land development banks.
